title: Clinical subphenotypes in septic patients with new-onset atrial fibrillation: validation and parsimonious classifier model development.
summary: Consensus hierarchical clustering of 1,535 MIMIC-IV sepsis patients with new-onset atrial fibrillation identified three subphenotypes; a nine-classifier pipeline was evaluated in 257 MIMIC-III patients. Weighted observational treatment associations do not establish causal treatment effects.
ai_technology: Consensus hierarchical clustering derives three sepsis/NOAF subphenotypes, and nine classifiers build a concise phenotype classifier.
organization: Department of Cardiology, Beijing Hospital, National Center of Gerontology, Institute of Geriatric Medicine, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, Beijing, China; Department of Anesthesiology, The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, China

evidence.tested: MIMIC-IV derivation (n=1,535) with MIMIC-III evaluation (n=257); retrospective treatment associations remain noncausal.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study
evidence.ai_role: Consensus hierarchical clustering derives three sepsis/NOAF subphenotypes, and nine classifiers build a concise phenotype classifier.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
